AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Although antithrombin (AT), protein C (PC), and antiplasmin (AP) are consumed during disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), their association with mortality in patients initially suspected of acute DIC is unknown. We examined how these proteins associate with mortality in consecutive patients initially suspected of DIC, fulfilling or not fulfilling overt DIC criteria.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: All consecutive patients clinically suspected of acute DIC during 5 years at a tertiary referral hospital were scored according to overt International Society of Thrombosis and Haemostasis (ISTH) DIC criteria. The influence of ISTH DIC score and measurements of AT, PC, and AP measured in all on mortality was assessed.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: During 1825 occurrences in 1814 patients, 91 fulfilled ISTH criteria for overt DIC (score ≥ 5). Both 28-day and 1-year mortality increased progressively as AT and in particular PC decreased. AT and PC correlated inversely with ISTH score (AT: R(2 ) = 0.14, P < 0.001, PC: R(2 ) = 0.21, P < 0.001). AP decreased when ISTH score of > 3 was reached. The 28-day mortality was 3%, 11%, 16%, 23%, 35%, and 52% and 1-year mortality 5%, 18%, 24%, 36%, 54%, and 63%, respectively for patients with an ISTH score of 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, and ≥5 (P < 0.001 for all).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Lowered AT and in particular PC activity was predictive of mortality risk upfront in critically ill patients suspected of acute DIC. Mortality in patients suspected of acute DIC increased progressively across the spectrum of the overt ISTH score and not only in those fulfilling overt DIC criteria.
